html:
The Rappahannock are an Algonquian-speaking people of eastern Virginia, named after the Rappahannock River where their towns stood when the English arrived. In the early 1600s they were one of the many groups that paid tribute to Powhatan, the paramount chief of the Tidewater.

John Smith met them in 1608 and marked their towns on his map of Virginia. As the Virginia colony spread up the river after the 1640s, they were pushed off their land and moved inland. Their neighbours on the river included the Cuttatawomen, Nandtaughtacund and Opiscopank. The Rappahannock Tribe lives on in King and Queen County and won federal recognition in 2018.
